what_happened: On 2026-11-04 the owner told the person running Athena to lift the per-agent spending and time caps "for now" because they were causing many failures. The change was queued as an urgent request to edit athena.toml. It raises the USD caps for the reader, writer, verifier, planner and critic, raises the writer and verifier time limits, and raises planning rounds from 3 to 5. It was a hand intervention outside any job. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed.
cause: Caps for each agent (money, time, planning rounds) are single fixed numbers in athena.toml. Athena does not record actual spend, duration or round counts per role against those numbers. It does not count how often each cap ends a job. It also does not separate a cap that is set too low from a plan or job that has grown. Earlier cases show this one role at a time: the producer deadline (raised from 1800 s to 3000 s), the job budget shortfall, and the timeout fix that needed urgent priority. Each time, a person saw the pattern and changed the numbers. Athena had no signal to propose a change. This time the whole set was lifted at once with no data on which cap caused the failures. Lifting all caps together also drops the cost protection the caps give, and nothing sets what to measure or when to put limits back ("for now" has no end).
prevention: Athena should record, for each job and each role, the spend, elapsed time and rounds used against the configured cap, and which cap ended the job. It should run a standing check that counts cap stops per role over a recent window. When one role passes a set share of stops, Athena should file a cap-review request itself. The request would include the measured percentiles and a proposed new value for that role only. Raises should be bounded: a cap may go up by a fixed multiple of the observed 90th percentile. A temporary lift should carry an expiry or a review date so it returns to a measured limit. This replaces blanket manual lifts with a targeted, data-backed change.
proposed_request: Add a cap-usage report and cap-review check to Athena. Outcome: (1) For every finished job, Athena records per role (reader, writer, verifier, planner, critic) the USD spent, seconds elapsed and planning rounds used, and which cap, if any, ended the run. These go in the job's records in the existing typed record format. (2) A command `athena caps` prints, per role over the last 30 jobs, the median and 90th percentile of spend and time, and the count and share of runs stopped by each cap. (3) When any role has 3 or more cap stops in the window, or over 20 percent of its runs stopped, Athena files one normal-priority cap-review request for that role. The request names the measured values and proposes a new cap no higher than 1.5 times the 90th percentile, and it does not file a second one while one is queued. (4) Any cap raise that the owner marks temporary carries a review date, and the check files a review request on that date. Acceptance: tests with fixture records built from real writer output show the report numbers, show a review filed at the threshold, and show no duplicate while one is queued. Do not change any cap values in athena.toml in this job.
